title: Tiny LSTM/GRU next-bar direction - OOS dir_acc ~ chance
hypothesis: Lagged return/vol features fed to a small LSTM/GRU can beat a logistic/ridge baseline on directional accuracy in walk-forward; costed Sharpe is the real score.
data: Default synthetic AR(1) daily returns (seed=42, n_bars=1200) from return-forecast-lstm; optional yfinance SPY not required for this note.
method: Walk-forward contiguous folds (train 400 / test 80); StandardScaler+logistic baseline vs 1-layer LSTM/GRU (hidden=16, seq_len=10); long/flat positions; 5 bps turnover cost; report IS vs OOS dir_acc / Sharpe / PnL.
result: On the synthetic AR(1) slice: LSTM OOS costed dir_acc ~ 0.47 (near chance), OOS costed Sharpe ~ -1.0 while IS costed Sharpe was positive (~0.39). GRU similarly weak OOS. Neither sequence model beats the logistic baseline OOS on directional accuracy (~0.47-0.49).
failure_reason: OOS directional accuracy collapses to coin-flip territory; IS/OOS Sharpe gap shows overfitting to fold noise on a weak AR(1) signal after costs. Tiny net + short sequences + turnover tax kill low-edge forecasts.
notes: RETROSPECTIVE NOTE citing metrics from the return-forecast-lstm README synthetic run table - not a live PnL claim.
